recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片中一顆白血球的細胞質內（箭頭）有一個圓形、帶透明外圈（莢膜樣光暈）的酵母菌體，符合被吞噬的隱球菌（Cryptococcus）。
features: Single leukocyte (phagocyte) with a dense, irregularly lobulated nucleus and pale, finely vacuolated cytoplasm
Intracytoplasmic round yeast form (arrow) with a central lavender body surrounded by a thin clear refractile halo, consistent with a capsule
A second, smaller faint round body appears adjacent to the arrowed organism, possibly another yeast or budding form
Background red cells are out of focus in a thick area of the smear; scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a leukocyte containing an intracytoplasmic round yeast form with a clear halo suggestive of a polysaccharide capsule (arrow); a second smaller round body is adjacent. No hyphae are seen, and the red cells are out of focus in this thick area, limiting assessment of the background. Findings are consistent with phagocytosed yeast, suggestive of disseminated Cryptococcus infection; confirmation by cryptococcal antigen testing, blood culture, and mucicarmine or India ink staining is recommended.

ddx.vs: Histoplasma yeasts are smaller (2-4 um), oval, and typically multiple within a phagocyte with a pseudocapsular clear space, whereas Cryptococcus is larger, round, variably sized, and often single with narrow-based budding.
Candida yeasts are small oval budding forms that often form pseudohyphae and lack a thick capsule.
An ingested red cell is pink-orange and homogeneous without a refractile capsular halo or budding.
A vacuole is empty and lacks the central stained yeast body surrounded by a defined wall.
